cases.courseBrief: UX Evidence-to-Prototype Capstone, a six-session project course in which students plan research, synthesize personas and journeys, model task flows, build testable prototypes, and combine accessibility conformance with observed usability evidence.
cases.qualityFocus: UX Evidence-to-Prototype Capstone, a six-session project course in which students plan research, synthesize personas and journeys, model task flows, build testable prototypes, and combine accessibility conformance with observed usability evidence.

lessonInput.title: Journey mapping
lessonInput.objectives: Use supplied claims to make a defensible distinction. Quality focus: UX Evidence-to-Prototype Capstone, a six-session project course in which students plan research, synthesize personas and journeys, model task flows, build testable prototypes, and combine accessibility conformance with observed usability evidence.
lessonInput.topics: Claim 0: Journey mapping represents an end-to-end experience from the user's perspective so a team can see connected steps, boundaries, breakdowns, and opportunities. Claim 1: A journey map should start from research about the steps users actually take and the transactions involved. Claim 2: An experience map should make struggle points and candidate improvement areas visible. Claim 3: A map can reveal dead ends where the user cannot continue toward the larger goal. Claim 4: Journey analysis should include gaps between online and offline parts of a service.

claims: Journey mapping represents an end-to-end experience from the user's perspective so a team can see connected steps, boundaries, breakdowns, and opportunities.
A journey map should start from research about the steps users actually take and the transactions involved.
An experience map should make struggle points and candidate improvement areas visible.
A map can reveal dead ends where the user cannot continue toward the larger goal.

anchors.quote: It's important for teams to make sure the thing they're building forms a coherent part of a user's wider journey.
Start by talking to your users to learn more about the steps they have to take and the transactions involved.
The map should show which bits of the journey users are struggling with and the areas you might want to focus on improving.
dead ends in the user journey
online and offline elements of the transaction not joining up in an intuitive way

cases.qualityFocus: Stress source coverage, answer-feedback consistency, misconception validity, key-term precision, and feedback instructionality. Explanations must correct the nearest sequence or boundary misconception, and choices must not collapse distinct observations into overlapping causal claims.

lessonInput.title: Plate tectonics as an Earth-system model
lessonInput.objectives: Use supplied claims to make a defensible distinction. Quality focus: Stress source coverage, answer-feedback consistency, misconception validity, key-term precision, and feedback instructionality. Explanations must correct the nearest sequence or boundary misconception, and choices must not collapse distinct observations into overlapping causal claims.
lessonInput.topics: Claim 0: Plate tectonics is the model that connects moving lithospheric plates with the origins of continents, oceans, mountains, earthquakes, volcanoes, and continental drift. Claim 1: The model explains features including folded rocks, mountain ranges, earthquakes, volcanoes, and continental drift. Claim 2: Earth's lithosphere consists of the crust and rigid outermost mantle and is divided into moving tectonic plates.
lessonInput.readings: Steven Earle, Physical Geology – 2nd Edition (2019), section 1.5, BCcampus Open Education

cases.courseBrief: Economics Models, Markets, and Evidence Lab, a twelve-session source-grounded course in which students interpret demand, elasticity, equilibrium, choice, inflation dynamics, natural experiments, circular flows, accumulation, proxy measures, labor-force categories, and opportunity cost.

lessonInput.title: Interactive prototyping
lessonInput.objectives: Use supplied claims to make a defensible distinction. Quality focus: UX Evidence-to-Prototype Capstone, a six-session project course in which students plan research, synthesize personas and journeys, model task flows, build testable prototypes, and combine accessibility conformance with observed usability evidence.
lessonInput.topics: Claim 0: Interactive prototyping builds a testable representation of how a planned experience looks and works without requiring every production detail. Claim 1: Prototypes can be combined with usability testing or a cognitive walkthrough to test whether a design concept works. Claim 2: Functional prototypes allow a team to observe how users interact with a product. Claim 3: A prototype should show the major interactions even when not every interaction is functional. Claim 4: Prototypes should support fast iteration and be inexpensive enough to discard after learning from them.

claims: Interactive prototyping builds a testable representation of how a planned experience looks and works without requiring every production detail.
Prototypes can be combined with usability testing or a cognitive walkthrough to test whether a design concept works.
Functional prototypes allow a team to observe how users interact with a product.
A prototype should show the major interactions even when not every interaction is functional.
Prototypes should support fast iteration and be inexpensive enough to discard after learning from them.

anchors.quote: A prototype is an interactive (high-fidelity) version of the experience you are planning to build. It shows how the design will look and work, without full detail.
Combined with other methods like usability testing or a cognitive walkthrough, prototypes help you test whether a design concept will work.
Functional prototypes help you observe how users interact with the product.
Show the major interactions. Not all interactions need to be functional.
Iterate. Prototypes should be quick to create and even quicker to discard.

lessonInput.topics: Claim 0: A variable is a name that refers to a stored value; the assignment operator = binds the name on the left to the value produced on the right (for objects it binds the reference, so no copy is made). Claim 1: A statement sets a variable to a value using the assignment operator (=), with the name on the left and the value on the right. Claim 2: Assignment is not mathematical equality — = copies a value into a variable rather than asserting two sides are equal. Claim 3: A variable name may contain letters, digits, and underscores and be any length, but cannot start with a digit. Claim 4: Variable names are case-sensitive, so total and Total are two different variables.
lessonInput.readings: OpenStax Introduction to Python Programming, §1.3 Variables

the loop body must make progress toward ending the condition

lessonInput.topics: Claim 0: A while loop repeatedly runs its body as long as a loop condition stays true, re-checking the condition before each iteration. anchors.quote: A while loop is a code construct that runs a set of statements, known as the loop body, while a given condition, known as the loop expression, is true
At each iteration, once the loop statement is executed, the loop expression is evaluated again
If true, the loop body will execute at least one more time. If false, the loop's execution will terminate
the loop body must make progress toward ending the condition

lessonInput.topics: Claim 0: Recursion solves a problem by reducing it to a simpler version of the same problem; a recursive function calls itself on a smaller input until it reaches a base case. lessonInput.topics: Claim 0: Interactive prototyping builds a testable representation of how a planned experience looks and works without requiring every production detail. Claim 1: Prototypes can be combined with usability testing or a cognitive walkthrough to test whether a design concept works. claims: Interactive prototyping builds a testable representation of how a planned experience looks and works without requiring every production detail.
Prototypes can be combined with usability testing or a cognitive walkthrough to test whether a design concept works.
Functional prototypes allow a team to observe how users interact with a product.
A prototype should show the major interactions even when not every interaction is functional.
Prototypes should support fast iteration and be inexpensive enough to discard after learning from them.

anchors.quote: A prototype is an interactive (high-fidelity) version of the experience you are planning to build. It shows how the design will look and work, without full detail.
Combined with other methods like usability testing or a cognitive walkthrough, prototypes help you test whether a design concept will work.
Functional prototypes help you observe how users interact with the product.
Show the major interactions. Not all interactions need to be functional.
Iterate. Prototypes should be quick to create and even quicker to discard.

cases.qualityFocus: Stress sign, direction, and representation boundaries. Separate field from force, potential from potential energy, current from charge, resistance from resistivity, electric from magnetic effects, flux from field strength, and Faraday induction from stored inductive energy. Require qualitative reasoning that is valid without inventing quantities absent from the source.

lessonInput.title: Conditionals and boolean logic
lessonInput.objectives: Use supplied claims to make a defensible distinction. Quality focus: Programming Decisions and Iteration, a six-session introductory Python workshop in which students trace short programs, explain state changes, and choose control-flow structures for concrete problems.
lessonInput.topics: Claim 0: A conditional statement chooses which block of code to run based on whether a condition is true; if-else takes exactly one branch, and boolean operators (and, or, not) build compound conditions. Claim 1: An if statement runs its body only when the condition is true, and skips it when the condition is false. Claim 2: An else clause holds statements that run when the if condition is false. Claim 3: and returns True only if both conditions are true; or returns True if either is true; not inverts a single condition.
lessonInput.readings: OpenStax Introduction to Python Programming, §4.2 If-else statements; §4.3 Boolean operations

anchors.quote: When an if-else statement is executed, one and only one of the branches is taken
If the condition is true, the body is executed. If the condition is false, the body is not executed
An else statement is used with an if statement and contains a body of statements that is executed when the if statement's condition is false
The and operator takes two condition operands and returns True if both conditions are true

attribution: OpenStax Introduction to Python Programming, §4.2 If-else statements; §4.3 Boolean operations

lessonInput.title: Circular flow of income
lessonInput.objectives: Use supplied claims to make a defensible distinction. Quality focus: Stress causal comparability, stock versus flow, proxy versus construct, unemployment versus nonparticipation, and explicit opportunity cost. Questions must remain answerable from supplied claims alone and explanations must rule out the strongest tempting alternative without adding policy facts.
lessonInput.topics: Claim 0: In the circular flow of income, money that households earn returns to firms as spending unless it leaks out of the flow as saving, taxes, or spending on imports. Claim 1: Leakages are balanced by injections such as investment, government spending, and exports that add spending back into the flow. Claim 2: When total leakages equal total injections, the circular flow is in balance and national income neither rises nor falls.

lessonInput.topics: Claim 0: Journey mapping represents an end-to-end experience from the user's perspective so a team can see connected steps, boundaries, breakdowns, and opportunities. Claim 1: A journey map should start from research about the steps users actually take and the transactions involved. Claim 2: An experience map should make struggle points and candidate improvement areas visible. Claim 3: A map can reveal dead ends where the user cannot continue toward the larger goal. Claim 4: Journey analysis should include gaps between online and offline parts of a service.

dead ends in the user journey
online and offline elements of the transaction not joining up in an intuitive way

lessonInput.title: Interactive prototyping
lessonInput.objectives: Use supplied claims to make a defensible distinction. Quality focus: Prototyping, Task Flow, and Accessibility, a six-session applied UX laboratory in which students diagram task decisions, build testable interactions, and combine conformance checks with observed user performance.
lessonInput.topics: Claim 0: Interactive prototyping builds a testable representation of how a planned experience looks and works without requiring every production detail. Claim 1: Prototypes can be combined with usability testing or a cognitive walkthrough to test whether a design concept works. Claim 2: Functional prototypes allow a team to observe how users interact with a product. Claim 3: A prototype should show the major interactions even when not every interaction is functional. Claim 4: Prototypes should support fast iteration and be inexpensive enough to discard after learning from them.

claims: Interactive prototyping builds a testable representation of how a planned experience looks and works without requiring every production detail.
Prototypes can be combined with usability testing or a cognitive walkthrough to test whether a design concept works.
Functional prototypes allow a team to observe how users interact with a product.
A prototype should show the major interactions even when not every interaction is functional.
Prototypes should support fast iteration and be inexpensive enough to discard after learning from them.

anchors.quote: A prototype is an interactive (high-fidelity) version of the experience you are planning to build. It shows how the design will look and work, without full detail.
Combined with other methods like usability testing or a cognitive walkthrough, prototypes help you test whether a design concept will work.
Functional prototypes help you observe how users interact with the product.
Show the major interactions. Not all interactions need to be functional.
Iterate. Prototypes should be quick to create and even quicker to discard.

anchors.quote: A prototype is an interactive (high-fidelity) version of the experience you are planning to build. It shows how the design will look and work, without full detail.

Functional prototypes help you observe how users interact with the product.
Show the major interactions. Not all interactions need to be functional.
Iterate. Prototypes should be quick to create and even quicker to discard.
